title: A morphogen gradient sets cell fates
caption: A morphogen spreads from its source and falls in concentration with distance. Cells read the concentration: above one threshold they take one fate, between the two thresholds another, below the lower one a third. One gradient can pattern a whole tissue, as Bicoid does along the fruit fly egg.
alt: A curve of morphogen concentration falling with distance from its source, with two horizontal thresholds dividing the tissue into three zones labelled fate A, fate B and fate C.
description: The morphogen is made at the left and its concentration falls with distance.
Cells where the concentration is above the upper threshold (0.6) take fate A.
Cells between the thresholds (0.6 and 0.25) take fate B.
Cells below the lower threshold (0.25) take fate C.
One gradient therefore makes three different cell types in order.
axisLabels: distance from the source of the morphogen
